testcase.name: the native renderer is at least as fast as the Java fallback
the atlas revision changes when new glyphs are rasterised
the glyphs are positioned relative to the baseline
an empty string has no width
a longer string is wider than a shorter one
unicode text is shaped into more than one glyph
the glyph atlas contains rasterised pixels
the native renderer can be closed and reports no glyphs afterwards
a longer string is wider than a shorter one
the native library reports its version
the shaped glyphs stay inside the measured width
measuring a string returns a positive width
the font exposes sane vertical metrics
the native and the Java renderer measure the same text equally
characters that the font does not contain are skipped
